purpose: Close the tempting fallback 'if degree three is silent, keep increasing the complete Boolean Macaulay degree until a refutation appears.' Modern Polynomial Calculus is already formulated with implicit multilinearization modulo x_i^2-x_i, matching the quotient-degree semantics used by v4.1. Known 3-colourability families require degree Omega(n) over every field. A complete multilinear Macaulay basis through linear degree has exponentially many squarefree monomials, and the cited degree-to-size results also give exponential PC proof size on these families.

proof_system_alignment.boolean_quotient: PC may be defined over the multilinear quotient F[x_1,...,x_n]/<x_i^2-x_i>, with multiplication followed by implicit multilinearization. This can only decrease degree/size relative to explicit Boolean-axiom reductions and is the convention used in modern degree-lower-bound work.
proof_system_alignment.consequence: The degree parameter in the lower-bound literature applies to the same multilinear monomial degree notion used by the v4.1 closure. The v4.1 success on small Tseitin/colouring controls is therefore compatible with asymptotic lower bounds; it is not a proof-system mismatch.

source_lower_bound.family: Sparse random regular graphs and sparse Erdos-Renyi graphs encoded by the standard Boolean 3-colourability CNF/polynomial system.
source_lower_bound.result: Conneryd, de Rezende, Nordstrom, Pang and Risse prove that Polynomial Calculus over any field asymptotically almost surely requires degree Omega(n) to refute 3-colourability for these sparse random graph families; via the standard size-degree relation this yields strongly exponential PC proof-size lower bounds.
source_lower_bound.scope: This is an existence/average-case worst-case barrier for PC, not an explicit deterministic graph family supplied by this artifact.

macaulay_dimension.definition: For N Boolean variables, the complete multilinear monomial space through degree d has D(N,d)=sum_{j=0}^d binom(N,j) coordinates.
macaulay_dimension.linear_degree: If d>=alpha*N for any fixed 0<alpha<=1/2, then D(N,d)>=binom(N,floor(alpha*N)).
macaulay_dimension.elementary_bound: For d=floor(alpha*N)>=1, binom(N,d)>= (N/d)^d. Thus for fixed alpha the dimension is at least (1/alpha)^(alpha*N-O(1))=2^(Omega(N)).
macaulay_dimension.algorithmic_meaning: An algorithm that materializes the complete Macaulay coefficient space up to the degree needed for these instances necessarily allocates exponentially many monomial coordinates.

theorem.name: ADAPTIVE_COMPLETE_MACAULAY_DEGREE_ESCALATION_IS_NOT_A_POLYNOMIAL_UNIVERSAL_ROUTE
theorem.statement: The strategy 'run complete multilinear Macaulay closure at degree 3,4,... until contradiction or completeness' cannot have polynomial worst-case complexity on arbitrary 3-CNF: there are width-O(1) Boolean families for which PC requires linear degree, while the complete degree-d squarefree monomial space is exponential at linear d.
proof: Use the source-backed family with required PC degree d>=alpha*N for a fixed alpha>0 along an infinite sequence of sizes.
Any complete Macaulay closure reaching a possible PC refutation must include degree at least d.
The number of squarefree monomial coordinates through this degree is D(N,d)>=binom(N,d)>=2^(Omega(N)).

Hence explicit complete-basis degree escalation is exponential before it can be complete on that family. The published size-degree implication independently gives strongly exponential PC proof size for the random-colouring instances.

killed: Promoting v4.1 to a universal algorithm by merely increasing a complete Macaulay degree while keeping all squarefree monomials through that degree.
Claiming that implicit Boolean multilinearization evades standard PC degree lower bounds.
Any implementation whose state explicitly contains the entire degree-d Boolean monomial basis when d must become linear.
not_killed: A non-PC proof system or contraction that implicitly aggregates high-degree information in polynomial state.
Formula-specific sparse high-degree certificates outside complete Macaulay enumeration, unless separately covered by proof-size lower bounds.

next_target.name: E8_HIGH_DEGREE_INFORMATION_WITHOUT_MONOMIAL_EXPANSION_V4_6
next_target.directive: Keep v4.1 as a strong polynomial preprocessor, but do not escalate complete degree. Seek a polynomial-size representation that transports genuinely high-degree/global information without listing monomials, affine intersections, assignments, or proof lines from a known exponential PC family. Candidate representations must come with exact zero/nonzero semantics, polynomial arithmetic bit complexity, and polynomial witness reconstruction.

sources: M. Miksa and J. Nordstrom, A Generalized Method for Proving Polynomial Calculus Degree Lower Bounds, Journal of the ACM 71(4), 2024. In particular, PC is formulated with implicit multilinearization modulo Boolean axioms.
J. Conneryd, S. F. de Rezende, J. Nordstrom, S. Pang, K. Risse, Graph Colouring Is Hard on Average for Polynomial Calculus and Nullstellensatz, FOCS 2023 / ECCC TR25-032 extended version.
